unit.subject: English
unit.unitOverview: In this unit you will learn about water — where it comes from, where we find it, and all the ways we use it every day. You will meet rainy and sunny weather, animals that live in water, and the big idea that water is a gift we should never waste. Say the words out loud — this is about confident English and being thankful for water, not perfect spelling.
unit.learningPath:
Begin with the guided teacher launch and learn a few words through pictures and play.
Listen to the Unit story and join in with repeated language.
Complete six language, speaking, early-writing and practical activities.
If you have access to live teacher sessions, meet your teacher three times each week for two weeks for extra practice — these are optional, and every skill in this unit is also fully covered through the teacher launch, story, and speaking and writing activities above.
Finish the ten-question checkpoint, then tell an adult what you can do if one is nearby — or say it out loud to yourself.

readings.title: The Well in the Village
readings.theme: water, weather, living things and care
readings.setting: Home, online lesson or Grade 1 classroom
readings.passageScript:
Amal lived in a small village. Near her house there was a deep well. The water in the well was cool and clean.

Every morning, Amal walked to the well with her big brother Adam. They carried an empty pot.

“Fill it slowly,” said Adam. “Water is precious. We must not waste one drop.”

Amal helped pull the rope. Up came the pot, full and heavy. “We did it!” she said.

At home, Mama used the water. “We use water to cook,” she said, making warm soup.

“And we use water to wash,” said Amal. She washed her hands until they were clean.

“And we use water to drink,” said little Hodan. She drank a big cup and smiled.

One day, the land was very dry. No rain came. The grass was brown. The plants did not grow.

“The well is getting low,” said Adam. “We must share and be careful.”

So the whole village shared the water. Nobody wasted a single drop.

Then, one afternoon, the sky went grey. Big clouds came. Drip… drip… drip…

“Rain!” shouted Amal. “It is raining!”

The children ran outside and danced in the rain. The rain filled the river. The rain filled the well.

The brown grass turned green again. The plants began to grow. The animals came to drink.

That night, Amal looked at the full well. “How lucky we are to have water,” she said softly. “Water is wonderful.”

quizzes.question: Which word is a water word?
quizzes.explanation: Rain is water falling from the clouds; a chair, a shoe and a book have nothing to do with water.

quizzes.question: Samira stood outside in the rain. How are her clothes now?
quizzes.explanation: Rain makes clothes wet; dry is the opposite, and hot and loud do not describe rainy clothes.

quizzes.question: Which word means the opposite of wet?
quizzes.explanation: Dry is the opposite of wet; rain, drop and float are all still to do with water.

quizzes.question: A leaf stays on top of the water. What is the leaf doing?
quizzes.explanation: Staying on top is called floating; sinking means going to the bottom.

quizzes.question: Sami drops a heavy stone into a bucket of water. What does it do?
quizzes.explanation: A heavy stone sinks to the bottom; only light things like a leaf float on top.

quizzes.question: Which of these needs water to stay alive?
quizzes.options: a spoon | a plant | a chair | a rock
quizzes.explanation: Plants are living and need water; a rock, a spoon and a chair are not alive.

quizzes.question: What falls from the clouds when it rains?
quizzes.explanation: Rain is drops of water from the clouds; sand, leaves and stones do not fall from clouds.

quizzes.question: What do we use water for before we eat?
quizzes.explanation: We wash with clean water before we eat; writing, reading and sleeping do not need water.

quizzes.question: Which is a good way to save water?
quizzes.options: Turn the tap off while you brush your teeth. | Leave the tap running all day. | Play with the hosepipe for hours. | Fill the bath right to the top.
quizzes.correctAnswer: Turn the tap off while you brush your teeth.
quizzes.explanation: Turning the tap off stops water being wasted; the other choices all waste a lot of water.

quizzes.question: Which sentence tells us about the weather?
quizzes.options: I am rainy today. | It is rainy today. | Today rainy is. | The rainy is today.
quizzes.explanation: We say it is for the weather; the other sentences have the words muddled up.

grownUpGuide.label: Teacher & Parent Guide
grownUpGuide.intro: In this unit, your child learns about water — where it comes from, where we find it, and all the ways we use it every day. They meet rainy and sunny weather, animals that live in water, and the big idea that water is a gift we should not waste. The goal is warm, confident English and a thankful heart for water — not perfect spelling.

sections.title: 🧭 About this unit (please read first)
sections.body:
Your child is a beginner, about 5–7 years old, and is just starting to read. So YOU lead this unit — a teacher in class or a parent at home.

Work in short, happy sessions of about 15–20 minutes. Lots of pointing, saying, singing, colouring and playing — very little writing.

This guide tells you what to do. The Child Activity Sheet is what your child draws and colours. The Story is one you read aloud.

sections.title: 💬 Using the AI Tutor with a young child
sections.body:
The grown-up holds the device and reads with the child — do not leave a 5-year-old alone with it.

Ask the tutor to say a word slowly so your child can copy the sound: “Please say the word ‘water’ slowly.”

Ask it to make the sound of rain, or to play a “does it float or sink?” guessing game with you and your child.

Ask it to give you one more simple water activity if your child wants to keep going.

sections.title: 🌟 Tips for teaching absolute beginners
sections.body:
Keep it short and playful. Stop while it is still fun.

Repeat, repeat, repeat — young children learn by hearing words many times.

Use real water when you can — a cup, a bowl, the tap, rain outside. Let them touch and pour.

Praise every try. Confidence matters more than being correct at this stage.

sections.title: Songs and Rhymes
sections.body:
The “Rainy Day” poem — say it together

Rain on the green grass. / Rain on the tree. / Rain on the houses / But not on me!

Wiggle your fingers like falling rain as you say it. Say it three times — a little louder each time!

“Row, Row, Row Your Boat” — sing and do the actions

Row, row, row your boat, / Gently down the stream. / Merrily, merrily, merrily, merrily, / Life is but a dream.

Sit facing your child, hold hands, and rock back and forth like rowing a boat.

sections.title: How to Teach This Unit, Step by Step
sections.body:
Repeat this simple shape over several short sessions:

1. Warm-up (2–3 min)

Greet your child in English: “Hello! How are you?”

Look outside together: “What is the weather like today? Is it sunny or rainy?”

2. Learn the words (5 min)

Point to real water (a cup, a tap, a puddle) and say the word clearly: “water”. Ask your child to repeat.

Do 4–5 words at a time. Use big smiles and lots of praise.

3. Play and sing (5 min)

Water Hunt: ask “Where do we find water?” and let your child point (tap, cup, rain, a picture of the sea).

Sing the “Rainy Day” poem and “Row Your Boat”, doing the actions together.

4. Story time (5 min)

Read the Story file, “The Well in the Village”, aloud. Point to the words in bold and to any pictures your child has drawn, and ask the simple talk-about questions.

5. Activity sheet (5 min)

Sit with your child and do one or two activities from the Child Activity Sheet. Read each instruction aloud for them.

6. Wrap-up (2 min)

Ask: “How did we use water today?” Celebrate! Say “Well done!” and remind them to say “Alhamdulillah” (thank you) for clean water.

sections.title: Sentence Patterns to Say Out Loud
sections.body: Speaking comes before writing. Practise these spoken patterns often:
items: “I use water to ______.” (drink, wash, cook)
“All living things need ______.” (water)
“We find water in the ______.” (river, sea, well)
“It is ______ today.” (rainy, sunny, cloudy)
“The ______ floats.” / “The ______ sinks.”

sections.title: Simple Check — What to Look For
sections.body: You do not need a test. Just watch and tick when your child can do these:
items: Says why we need water.
Names 3 places we find water (rain, river, sea, well).
Says one way they use water: “I use water to ______.”
Names 2 animals that live in water.
Joins in the “Rainy Day” poem or “Row Your Boat”.
